clue.text: Source of year abroad in French region

indicators.note: in tells us the year goes inside the region's name

parts.note: Provence is the region of south-eastern France
an is the French word for year, so abroad it is AN

explanation.surface: A student's paperwork on where they spent a gap year in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' asks for a foreign word: French 'an' (year) sits inside PROVENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the provenance of something is its origin or place it came from, especially for artworks.

clue.text: Father's art being curious?

parts.note: a Catholic father is a cleric; archaic 'thou pryest' means 'thou art being curious', and pryest is said like the clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dad's painting is rather strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting but the old form of 'are': 'thou pryest' = 'thou art being curious', which sounds like the title of a Father.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Catholic clergyman is addressed as Father, so the clerical title fits the first word.

clue.text: Wildcat strike ending great deal after company goes belly-up

indicators.note: after places the strike's ending and the great deal behind the flipped company
in a down clue turning belly-up flips the letters so they read upwards
ending picks out just the final letter of the word strike

parts.note: a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: An unofficial walkout ends a big agreement once the firm collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildcat strike' looks like industrial action, but 'Wildcat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ocelot is a wild feline of Central and South America.

clue.text: Former partner looked after kids — and the rest!

definitions.text: Former partner looked after kids — and the rest!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
tended means looked after
a couple's family is their children

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse minding the children, plus everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: children plus grandparents, aunts, cousins and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the wider kin group beyond parents and children, including all other relatives.

clue.text: Love a geeky type, one turning up that'll get heart pounding

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the whole string reads from bottom to top

parts.note: love is a score of zero, nil
a nerd is a geeky person
one can be the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: Romance with a nerd: something to set the pulse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses the whole string NILANERDA, giving the answer read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the hormone released under stress makes the pulse race.

clue.text: Telegraph lead

definitions.meaning: to send a telegram, to wire a message

explanation.surface: A newspaper's top story.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a telegram sent by wire, and a wire or flex connecting a device.

clue.text: Press head removed in clearout of opponents

indicators.note: head removed means the first letter of the purge word is dropped

parts.note: a purge rids a party of its opponents

explanation.surface: A political purge where a leader is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to press someone is to urge them to act.

clue.text: Suggesting fast over?

parts.note: to do something over is to redo it
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Hinting that the fast has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' means 'do over' and 'fast' is a period without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: redolent of something means suggesting or evoking it.

clue.text: Recipient has choice between death and high office

parts.note: end can mean death
or offers a choice
a see is a bishop's seat of office

explanation.surface: An heir chooses between dying and high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' places the choice word inside the other two; a see is a bishop's diocese, the seat of high church office.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the payee to whom a cheque is endorsed receives it.

clue.text: Who'll secure man-hours after reorganisation?

indicators.note: reorganisation means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which department will find staff time once restructuring is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the personnel department hires staff and so supplies working hours.

clue.text: Italian team's centre backs being sluggish

indicators.note: the middle letter of the club name goes to the back

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club

explanation.surface: A football report on a slow Inter Milan defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre backs' looks like defenders but says the centre letter T moves to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inert means motionless or slow to move, sluggish.

clue.text: Spring grass outside recovered quickly

indicators.note: outside says the grass wraps round the spring

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Springtime grass outdoors bounced back fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that rebounded bounced back, recovering swiftly.

clue.text: Exhausted cohabiting? Prepared to govern

definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: worn (exhausted) placed in sin, since cohabiting was once called living in sin
having taken the oath of office before taking power

explanation.surface: Is a tired couple living together ready to rule?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cohabiting?' is 'living in sin': the tired word lives inside the sin, so the first half is a playful second definition rather than standard wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: officials who have taken their oath of office are ready to take power.

clue.text: One expecting net profit to recount returns, getting head of investment in

indicators.note: in puts that first letter inside the turned word
returns signals reading the recount word backwards

parts.note: to relate a story is to recount it

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of investment

explanation.surface: An investor wanting a net gain recounts the returns.
explanation.walkthrough: RELATE turned round gives ETALER; I goes inside. 'Net' means the internet, not after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an online seller expects to make money through the internet.

clue.text: Aggression of drunken reeling celeb

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk celebrity staggering about and turning nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belligerence is hostile, combative behaviour.

clue.text: Grand ancient heraldic device, a bird

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
ancient means old
a crest is an emblem in heraldry

explanation.surface: A grand old coat of arms featuring a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the goldcrest is Europe's smallest songbird.

clue.text: Secret rite performed in Eastern society

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside society
performed suggests the rite's letters being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A hidden ritual carried out by an oriental club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performed' anagrams the rite to TERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, hence secret.

clue.text: Retired Australian runner's holding flag aloft

indicators.note: holding means the bird contains the turned word

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird that runs; 's adds S

indicators.note: in a down clue aloft means read upwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: An Australian athlete raises a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is a verb meaning tire; 'aloft' reverses it to ERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: emeritus describes a professor or official retired but keeping an honorary title.

clue.text: One who's had some successful knockouts concealing broken nail in two fingers?

definitions.text: One who's had some successful knockouts

indicators.note: concealing means the half-fist hides the broken nail inside

parts.note: two fingers curled are half a fist, playfully a semi-fist

indicators.note: broken says the nail's letters are smashed into another order

explanation.surface: A boxer who has won by knockouts hides a damaged nail in a partial fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' turns NAIL into INAL. 'Knockouts' are elimination rounds, not punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone who reaches the last four has won earlier knockout rounds.

clue.text: Government representative's odd turn of phrase

indicators.note: an odd turn suggests the letters being twisted into a strange order

explanation.surface: An official's peculiar choice of wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' looks like an idiom, but 'odd turn of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialist sense: an official who prepares summit talks for a head of government is called this, after Himalayan guides.

clue.text: A West Midlands town more than semi skilled

parts.words: West Midlands town more than semi
parts.note: Droitwich is a spa town in Worcestershire in the English West Midlands; more than half its name, five of nine letters, is kept

explanation.surface: A semi-skilled worker in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi' looks attached to 'skilled' but goes with 'more than': keep the first five of Droitwich's nine letters, dropping WICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adroit means deft and clever, skilful.

clue.text: Broth I'm cooking clots

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters being stirred and mixed

explanation.surface: Making soup that turns lumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: thrombi are blood clots forming in vessels.

clue.text: State expression of objection when interrupting wedding speech

indicators.note: interrupting puts the objection inside the vow

parts.note: 'I do' is the vow at a wedding
ah can voice protest

explanation.surface: Someone objects in the middle of a wedding vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Brought up fish, absurdly huge to be caught

indicators.note: to be caught puts the jumbled letters within the fish

parts.note: the cod is a fish

indicators.note: absurdly suggests the letters of huge in a nonsensical order

explanation.surface: An angler hauling up a ridiculously large catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have coughed something is to have brought it up from the throat.

clue.text: Get back 13, the army's coming in — get back!

indicators.note: coming in puts the army inside the turned word
get back tells the cross-referenced word to go into reverse

parts.note: 13 points to the answer at 13 across, the online seller
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An order to the army to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back!' reverses the 13-across answer to RELIATE; the army goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get back at someone is to take revenge, strike in return.

clue.text: It's an oddity, masculinised papal court?

indicators.note: Latin and Italian feminine -a endings become masculine -o

parts.note: the Curia is the papal court of the Vatican

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a male-dominated Vatican is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masculinised' swaps the feminine ending A for masculine O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a curio is a rare or unusual object, a curiosity.

clue.text: Trophy held in second division

indicators.note: held in means the trophy keeps second inside

parts.note: a cup is a sports trophy

explanation.surface: A cup won by a second-division team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second division' reads as a league, but 'division' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: a cusp is the dividing point between two zodiac signs or states.

clue.text: One taking part in match between two opponents (not international)

indicators.note: not removes the international's letter
between puts the match between the two opponents

parts.note: con and anti both mean against, as in pros and cons
a test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A match between two sides, but not an international one.
explanation.walkthrough: CON and ANTI flank TEST, then 'not international' drops the I of ANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a contestant is a competitor taking part in a contest.
